Subject: Exec clearance request: 3-year rate anchor + renewal protection (Solstice Health)

Laura / Jordan —

Quick ask: Solstice Health (POC: Maya Patel) is at final terms but is requesting a 3-year rate anchor with renewal protection language and an uplift cap. This is outside standard guardrails for our standard 12-month MSA. Reasoning below and ask at the bottom.

Summary (proposal):
- Term: 36 months initial term
- Price anchor: fixed per-token price for first 24 months; thereafter annual uplift capped at +4% for remaining 12 months
- Renewal protection: if Solstice expands materially (>20% ARR increase) we reserve right to reprice on incremental usage only; base committed ARR locked per term
- Discount: 22% off list across generation + embeddings for committed volume (3yr commit: $4.2M ARR)

Business rationale: Solstice is in production with a pilot (billing live) and expects rapid volume growth if we can guarantee predictable unit economics. They are requesting multi-year stability to support budget approval from their board. This is a strategic vertical reference — healthcare data handling requirements mean this could unlock other healthcare prospects.

Risks / asks:
- This is below our Playbook floor for >1yr commitments (they qualify for Strategic Partner path)
- We need signoff on the renewal protection language (legal redlines attached) and a final exec clearance for the uplift cap and 3yr anchor

Attachments: Solstice_TermSheet_v3.pdf (term sheet), pricing-model.xlsx (forecast)

Requested approval: "Approve as-is" or "Approve with constraints" (specify constraints) — ideally by EOD Wed so we can finalize DocuSign link to their procurement.

Thanks —
Aditya
Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: Exec clearance request: 3-year rate anchor + renewal protection (Solstice Health)

Laura / team — attaching redlines and short notes. Major items:

- Auto-renew: Solstice's legal added an automatic renewal provision tied to CPI; we replaced with a mutual renewal notice window and a 30-day priced-extension fallback.
- Renewal protection: redlines restrict the protection to the committed ARR and define "expansion" thresholds we can reprice. Per our standard it's reasonable to cap repricing to incremental usage over the committed baseline.
- Escrow / Price Escrow: Legal recommends a short escrow clause for multi-year price protection (limited use) vs. a full escrow mechanism — this protects both parties.

See attached: redlines-markup.docx (comments inline).

Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
(attachment: redlines-markup.docx)
